etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English used, equivalent to use +‎ -ed.

definitions.definition: simple past and past participle of use

quote.citation: 1948, Carey McWilliams, North from Mexico / The Spanish-Speaking People of The United States, J. B. Lippincott Company, page 75:
quote.text: In 1866 Colonel J. F. Meline noted that the rebozo had almost disappeared in Santa Fe and that hoop skirts, on sale in the stores, were being widely used.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, auxiliary, defective, only in past tense/participle) To perform habitually; to be accustomed [to doing something].
That is or has or have been used.

quote.citation: 2013 August 3, “Boundary problems”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8847:
quote.text: Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too. GDP measures the total value of output in an economic territory. Its apparent simplicity explains why it is scrutinised down to tenths of a percentage point every month.

definitions.definition: That has or have previously been owned by someone else.

quote.citation: 1965, Bob Dylan, Like a Rolling Stone:
quote.text: Nobody's ever taught you how to live out on the street and now you're gonna have to get used to it.
